knowledge:
- key_parameters:
    - DEtype=Specifies the upstream differential expression analysis tool used to generate the input data (e.g., "limma", "edgeR", "edger", "DESeq2", "prescored").
    - geneTable=A two-column data frame mapping probe or gene identifiers in the profiling data to those in the gene sets (essential for methylation arrays or custom gene accessions).
    - geneIDcol=The name of the column containing gene identifiers if they are not present as row names in the input data frame.
    - joinType=Determines how multiple contrasts are merged; default is to include only genes detected in all contrasts, but can be set to "full" for sparse data.
    - priority=Prioritization method for enrichment results; "significance" prioritizes by small adjusted p-values, while "effect" prioritizes by the magnitude of the enrichment score (s.dist).
    - cores=Number of parallel threads to use for calculation (default is 1; higher values like 8-12 speed up calculation but require more RAM).
    - minsetsize=Minimum number of gene set members present in the profiling data required to retain a gene set (default is 10).
    - resrows=Number of top gene sets used to generate charts in downstream visualization (default is 50).
    - overwrite=Logical value indicating whether to overwrite an existing HTML report file in mitch_report().
    - FDR=False Discovery Rate threshold for filtering gene sets in network plots.
    - n_sets=Number of top gene sets to display in network plots.
- alternatives:
    - Over-representation analysis (ORA) based approaches for methylation data, which the documentation notes appear to lack sensitivity compared to mitch's rank-MANOVA approach.
- when_to_use:
    - Pathway analysis of profiling studies with one, two, or more contrasts.
    - Multi-omics studies (e.g., proteomic, transcriptomic, and epigenomic analysis of the same samples).
    - Pathway-level differential analysis of single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data.
    - Pathway analysis of Infinium Methylation array data (HM450K or EPIC) by aggregating probe-level t-statistics to gene-level scores.
- pitfalls:
    - Old annotations for HM450K and EPIC arrays contain obsolete gene names (~12-13%), so gene symbols should be updated using HGNChelper before enrichment analysis.
    - Enrichments with large effect sizes may not be statistically significant when prioritizing by "effect".
    - When prioritizing by "significance", large effect sizes might be missed.
    - Using more CPU threads (cores) requires more RAM, so system memory must be monitored.
    - Network plots work best when the width is double the height to prevent long gene set names from being cut off.
    - There is stochasticity in the network projection, so it may need to be repeated for a nice layout.

workflows.name: standard_multi_contrast_enrichment
workflows.intent: Perform multi-contrast pathway enrichment analysis on differential expression data (e.g., RNA-seq) using gene sets from a GMT file.
input: rna (differential expression data frame from edgeR)
k9a (differential expression data frame from edgeR)
workflows.stages:
1. Import gene sets from a GMT file using gmt_import.
2. Import and merge multi-contrast profiling data using mitch_import.
3. Calculate multivariate enrichment using mitch_calc.
4. Generate an interactive HTML report using mitch_report.
5. Generate high-resolution PDF plots using mitch_plots.
6. Visualize gene set similarity and driver genes using networkplot and network_genes.
workflows.code:
download.file("https://reactome.org/download/current/ReactomePathways.gmt.zip",
    destfile="ReactomePathways.gmt.zip")
unzip("ReactomePathways.gmt.zip")
genesets <- gmt_import("ReactomePathways.gmt")
data(rna,k9a)
x <- list("rna"=rna,"k9a"=k9a)
y <- mitch_import(x,"edgeR")
res <- mitch_calc(y,genesetsExample,priority="effect",cores=2)
mitch_report(res,"myreport.html",overwrite=TRUE)
mitch_plots(res,outfile="mycharts.pdf")
networkplot(res,FDR=1,n_sets=10)
network_genes(res,FDR=1,n_sets=10)

workflows.name: methylation_array_enrichment
workflows.intent: Perform pathway enrichment analysis on Infinium Methylation array data (HM450K or EPIC) by aggregating probe-level differential methylation statistics to gene-level scores.
input: dma3a.tsv (differential probe methylation results from limma)
workflows.stages:
1. Retrieve probe-to-gene annotations from the array annotation package.
2. Format and clean the probe-to-gene mapping table.
3. Update deprecated gene symbols using HGNChelper.
4. Import probe-level differential methylation data and aggregate to gene-level scores using mitch_import.
5. Calculate pathway enrichment using mitch_calc.
6. Generate high-resolution PDF plots using mitch_plots.
7. Generate an interactive HTML report using mitch_report.
8. Visualize gene set similarity and driver genes using networkplot and network_genes.
workflows.code:
library("IlluminaHumanMethylation450kanno.ilmn12.hg19")
anno <- getAnnotation(IlluminaHumanMethylation450kanno.ilmn12.hg19)
myann <- data.frame(anno[,c("UCSC_RefGene_Name","UCSC_RefGene_Group","Islands_Name","Relation_to_Island")])
gp <- myann[,"UCSC_RefGene_Name",drop=FALSE]
gp2 <- strsplit(gp$UCSC_RefGene_Name,";")
names(gp2) <- rownames(gp)
gp2 <- lapply(gp2,unique)
gt1 <- stack(gp2)
colnames(gt1) <- c("gene","probe")
gt1$probe <- as.character(gt1$probe)
new.hgnc.table <- readRDS("../inst/extdata/new.hgnc.table.rds")
fix <- checkGeneSymbols(gt1$gene,map=new.hgnc.table)
gt1$gene <- fix$Suggested.Symbol
x <- read.table("https://ziemann-lab.net/public/gmea/dma3a.tsv",header=TRUE,row.names=1)
y <- mitch_import(x,DEtype="limma",geneTable=gt1)
res<-mitch_calc(y,genesetsExample,priority="effect",cores=2,minsetsize=5)
mitch_plots(res,outfile="methcharts.pdf")
mitch_report(res,"methreport.html")
networkplot(res,FDR=0.1,n_sets=10)
network_genes(res,FDR=1,n_sets=10)
